t:
(a) Strategy Required.—The Secretary of Defense shall develop and implement a strategy for developing and sustaining through fiscal year 2020 information operations capabilities for future contingencies. The Secretary shall submit such strategy to the congressional defense committees by not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act. 
    (b) Contents of Strategy.—The strategy required by subsection (a) shall include each of the following:
        (1) A plan for the sustainment of existing capabilities that have been developed during the ten-year period prior to the date of the enactment of this Act, including such capabilities developed using funds authorized to be appropriated for overseas contingency operations determined to be of enduring value for continued sustainment. 
        (2) A discussion of how the capabilities referred to in paragraph (1) are integrated into policy, doctrine, and operations. 
        (3) An assessment of the force structure that is required to sustain operational planning and potential contingency operations, including the integration across the active and reserve components. 
        (4) Estimates of the steady-state resources needed to support the force structure referred to in paragraph (3), as well as estimates for resources that might be needed based on selected operational plans, contingency plans, and named operations. 
        (5) An assessment of the impact of how new and emerging technologies can be incorporated into policy, doctrine, and operations. 
        (6) A description of ongoing research into new capabilities that may be needed to fill any identified gaps and programs that might be required to develop such capabilities. 
        (7) Potential policy implications or legal challenges that may prevent the integration of new and emerging technologies into the projected force structure. 
        (8) Potential policy implications or challenges to the better leveraging of capabilities from interagency partners.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that submitting a strategy to congressional committees, or the reference to "interagency partners", amounts to consultation. Both Congress and interagency partners are inside the federal government, so neither crosses the federal boundary. The section only directs the Secretary of Defense to develop an internal strategy and report it to Congress, with no public comment, rulemaking, advisory body with outside members, or consultation with states, tribes, experts, or the public.
fable.s: The Secretary shall submit such strategy to the congressional defense committees by not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act.

qwen_block.w: This section requires the Secretary of Defense to develop a strategy and submit it to congressional defense committees. Congress and its committees are part of the federal government, so reporting to them is an internal government action, not participation by outside parties. There is no requirement for consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary shall submit such strategy to the congressional defense committees by not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act.

opus.w: The only formal interactions in this section are the Secretary submitting a strategy to the congressional defense committees and the strategy discussing "interagency partners." Both stay inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, and there is no comment period, hearing, or right to sue. The submission to Congress may look like participation, but a report to Congress does not count under the definition.
opus.s: The Secretary shall submit such strategy to the congressional defense committees by not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Secretary of Defense to develop a strategy and submit a report to congressional defense committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is not participation. The mention of 'interagency partners' refers to other federal agencies, which are also inside the federal government. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with any non-federal entities.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary shall submit such strategy to the congressional defense committees by not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act.
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it mentions "interagency partners" and "integration across the active and reserve components," which might imply coordination with outside entities.
Resolution: "Interagency partners" refers to other federal agencies (inside the government), and "active and reserve components" refers to military branches (inside the government). The section requires a report to Congress (inside the government). There is no requirement to consult with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
